decisions.reason: The polymer concrete drain housing has its own page and is a core installation component that fits the firm's compatible product families, so the firm is committed to it and will keep it.
Floor-level shower drainage is central to the direction the firm has announced, so even modest visibility gives management reason to persist with the line.
As the publicly presented flagship of the firm's design-focused direction, the designer shower drain carries heavy investment and visible commitment, so dropping it is very unlikely.
The shower element with integrated slope supports the low-profile, integrated bathroom strategy, and any weak early results can still be put down to market ramp-up after only one year.
The backflow-protected basement drain has its own page and a specific launch announcement, which makes it a visible public commitment, so it will be kept.
The air-admittance valve is more peripheral and only mentioned on the website, but it is cheap to keep in the range and complements the drainage systems, so it stays for now.
